items.text: For decades. <break time="0.8s" /> Companies have treated data like a sealed box. <break time="0.8s" /> ― valuable, private, and tightly protected. <break time="0.8s" /> That instinct made sense. <break time="0.8s" /> What was inside the box. <break time="0.8s" /> ― customer histories, operational insights, proprietary knowledge ―. <break time="0.8s" /> Represented control and competitive advantage. <break time="0.8s" /> In an industrial economy. <break time="0.8s" /> Owning data was power. <break time="0.8s" /> But in the Intelligence Age. <break time="0.8s" /> That logic is becoming an obstacle. <break time="0.8s" /> Value no longer comes primarily. <break time="0.8s" /> From keeping information. <break time="0.8s" /> But from connecting it. <break time="0.8s" /> ― across functions, partners, and ecosystems ―. <break time="0.8s" /> To enable learning and action in real time. <break time="0.8s" /> Holding on to the sealed box today. <break time="0.8s" /> Is less like safeguarding an asset. <break time="0.8s" /> And more like dragging an anchor. <break time="0.8s" /> The companies moving fastest. <break time="0.8s" /> Are not just opening the box. <break time="0.8s" /> They are doing something more deliberate. <break time="0.8s" /> Opening it just enough. <break time="0.8s" /> To allow data to move, combine, and learn. <break time="0.8s" /> ― securely, selectively, and with purpose. <break time="0.8s" /> The objective is not openness for its own sake. <break time="0.8s" /> But smart connection to gain an edge.
